update.title: [RISC-V] Remove obsolete, never taken to silicon xventanacondops extension
update.body:
This patch removes the xventanacondops support from GCC.  It was something I
meant to do last cycle, but never got around to it.

xventanacondops was specific to the first generation Ventana design which we
ultimately decided to shelve for various reasons.  It was never taken to
silicon by anyone.  zicond provides the exact same functionality, but is
standardized by RVI and naturally sits in a different encoding space.

I'm keen to avoid keeping around code which will never be used.  Given the
design never made it to silicon, I don't really even see the point in keeping
the options lying around for compatibility purposes.  As a result this is a
complete removal.

Tested on riscv32-elf and riscv64-elf.  Bootstraps on the various designs will
happen tonight as part of the regular cycle.

update.title: RISC-V: Add -z zicfilp=, -z zicfiss= and the CFI report options
update.body:
Add the linker options for the Zicfilp and Zicfiss GNU properties
defined by the RISC-V toolchain conventions [1], with the same meaning
as in lld:

  -z zicfilp=[implicit|unlabeled|never]
  -z zicfilp-unlabeled-report=[none|warning|error]
  -z zicfiss=[implicit|always|never]
  -z zicfiss-report=[none|warning|error]

`implicit` is the default, so the output has a property only if all
inputs have it.  `unlabeled` and `always` set the property on the output,
and `never` clears it.

The `report` options are independent of the marking options, and report
nothing by default.

[1] https://github.com/riscv-non-isa/riscv-toolchain-conventions/pull/186
update.author: kito-cheng

update.title: [RISC-V] Fix remaining AOP related regressions on the RISC-V port
update.body:
On RISC-V steering for AOP sometimes should steer towards PLUS, other times
towards IOR.  For example we want PLUS because we have shadd style insns that
we can form and PLUS sometimes compresses better.  Sometimes we want IOR
because we can generate single bit manipulations.  Things are made a bit more
complicated by supporting rv32, rv64 and the various relevant extensions.

Generally if all the arguments are registers, steer towards PLUS if ZBA is
enabled.  Otherwise steer towards IOR.  The additional wrinkle here is that
there aren't sub-word logicals on rv64, so we have to pun them to DImode and
emit a 64bit operation.

This fixes the pr80770-2 regression on both riscv32-elf and riscv64-elf and the
pr58727 and pr93504 failures on riscv64-elf and is enough to make everything
happy again.  Bootstrapped and regression tested on the k3 and c920 (k1 in
progress).

gcc/
	* config/riscv/riscv.md (aop<mode>3): New expander.
update.author: Jeff Law

update.title: [RISC-V] Fix pr58727 code quality regression on RISC-V
update.body:
Essentially we have an outer IOR with turns on one or more bits that were
masked off by an inner AND.  Previously we'd potentially turn those bits back
on in the AND mask in the hopes the constant would simplify (ideally into a
single bit clear constant).  So instead of bclr+ior were now getting
and+bclr+plus (and clears low bits, bclr clears a high bit, plus turns on the
just cleared low bits).

The steering towards PLUS broke that code.  I tried to fix in simplify-rtx, but
things kept getting mucked up as we bubbled out of the various SUBST and
simplification calls in combine which is unfortunate as other ports that are
limited to single bit manipulation rather than generalized bitfields could
benefit.  Also note that since we're dropping that inner AND, we have to change
the outer operation back to IOR to keep the semantics correct.

After much head-banging I gave in and implemented it in the RISC-V backend ;(

Bootstrapped and regression tested on the c920 and k3 (k1 is in progress).
Also regression tested on riscv32-elf and riscv64-elf.

gcc/
	* config/riscv/bitmanip.md: Add new 3->2 splitter when an outer PLUS
	turns on some bits cleared by an inner AND.  Adjust the AND mask and
	change the outer code to IOR.

update.title: xtensa: compare SEC_MERGE literals by their merged addresses
update.body:
When two literals hold the same value, the Xtensa linker keeps only
one of them.  It decided two literals were the same if they pointed
to the same offset in the same input section.

That is wrong for mergeable string sections (SEC_MERGE), because the
linker may move strings while merging duplicates.  Two references
that start at the same offset can end up at different addresses.

Example:

    .section .rodata.str1.1,"aMS",@progbits,1
  .LC0:
    .string "{\"v\":7}"     # offset 0, 8 bytes
  .LC1:
    .string "v"             # offset 8

    .literal .Lend, .LC0+8  # one past the end of .LC0
    .literal .Lkey, .LC1

Both literals point to input offset 8.  If "v" is merged with a copy
in another file, .LC1 moves but .LC0+8 does not.  The linker merged
the two literals anyway, so code that loaded .Lkey got the address
after "{\"v\":7}" instead of "v".

Now compare the addresses the references will have after merging.
The assembler writes references in two forms, and they move
differently:

  - "section + offset": the offset picks a string, so look up where
    that string went.
  - "symbol + addend": look up where the symbol went, then add the
    addend.

relocate_section and the RISC-V relaxation code compute addresses the
same way.

	* elf32-xtensa.c (r_reloc_merged_offset): New.
	(literal_value_equal): Use it for SEC_MERGE sections.

	* testsuite/ld-xtensa/coalesce-merge.t,
	* testsuite/ld-xtensa/coalesce-merge-1.s,
	* testsuite/ld-xtensa/coalesce-merge-2.s: New test.
	* testsuite/ld-xtensa/xtensa.exp: Run it.

update.title: RISC-V: Introduce TLSDESC relaxation.
update.body:
In an executable, always turn a TLSDESC access into IE, or into LE when
the symbol is local.

When the sequence has R_RISCV_RELAX, the relax pass deletes the first
two instructions.  Only the 2 instruction (long) forms are done for now:

  auipc a0, <hi>            lui  a0, <hi>
  l[dw] a0, <lo>(a0)        addi a0, a0, <lo>

Otherwise, for example with -mno-relax or --no-relax, rewrite the
sequence in place without changing its size, like lld does:

  auipc tX, %tlsdesc_hi(sym)            nop
  l[dw] tY, %tlsdesc_load_lo(.L)(tX)    nop
  addi  a0, tX, %tlsdesc_add_lo(.L)     auipc a0, <hi>  /  lui  a0, <hi>
  jalr  t0, tY, %tlsdesc_call(.L)       l[dw] a0, <lo>(a0)  /  addi a0, a0, <lo>

This makes TLSDESC work in static executables, where nothing can
resolve a TLS descriptor at run time.

update.title: RISC-V: Update the unlabeled landing pad PLT to the latest psABI
update.body:
The psABI landing pad PLT [1] loads the target address into t2 and
jumps through it, both in the PLT entries and in the PLT header.  A
jump through t2 (x7) is a software guarded branch under Zicfilp, so
its target does not need to start with a landing pad.

Update the unlabeled landing pad PLT to match the psABI:

- The PLT entries use t2 instead of t3.
- The PLT header swaps t2 and t3.
- The PLT header no longer starts with a landing pad, because the PLT
  entries reach it through t2.  It also drops the three trailing nops,
  so it is 32 bytes, the same size as the default PLT header.

  PLT header:
    1:	auipc  t3, %pcrel_hi(.got.plt)
	sub    t1, t1, t2
	l[w|d] t2, %pcrel_lo(1b)(t3)
	addi   t1, t1, -(hdr size + 16)
	addi   t0, t3, %pcrel_lo(1b)
	srli   t1, t1, log2(16/PTRSIZE)
	l[w|d] t0, PTRSIZE(t0)
	jr     t2

  PLT entry:
	lpad   0
    1:	auipc  t2, %pcrel_hi(function@.got.plt)
	l[w|d] t2, %pcrel_lo(1b)(t2)
	jalr   t1, t2

NOTE: This change is backward compatible since the PLT are generated by
the linker, and the linker will generate the new PLT header and entries.

[1] https://github.com/riscv-non-isa/riscv-elf-psabi-doc/pull/417
update.author: kito-cheng

update.title: RISC-V: Fix the implied extensions of xsmtvdotii
update.body:
riscv_implicit_subsets is walked only once, so an extension must come
before the extensions it implies.  xsmtvdotii implies xsmtvdot, but it
was listed after it, so -march=rv64i_xsmtvdotii got xsmtvdot without the
zve32x that xsmtvdot implies.

Swap the two entries, and add xsmtvdot and xsmtvdotii to the imply test.

update.title: OpenMP: Add the 'scaled' modifier to the 'simdlen' clause [PR127723]
update.body:
This OpenMP 6.1 (TR14) feature was added to handle the fancier
simdlen variants of AArch64/RISC-V.

Namely, besides 'simdlen(length)' there is now also an optional scale
factor:
  simdlen( scaled(arith-type [, divisor]) : length )
with the scaling factor defaulting to one when absent and otherwise being
  max(1, round_down(VL(type) / divisor))
and VL(type) is a target & type specific value, which might be only
known at runtime (divisor and length must be >= 1 and constant).
And 'type' is an arithmetic type (C/C++) or numeric intrinsic type
(Fortran).

The 'simdlen' with 'scaled' can be specified on 'declare simd', on
the 'simd' directive and - as context selector - on 'declare variant'.

This commit adds support for C and C++, only, and currently fails with
a sorry in gimplify_scan_omp_clauses and simd_clone_clauses_extract.

	PR middle-end/127723

gcc/ChangeLog:

	* attribs.cc (omp_declare_simd_clauses_equal): Handle
	simdlen's type and divisor of the scaled modifier.
	* omp-general.cc (resolve_omp_target_device_matches,
	omp_construct_simd_compare): Likewise.
	* gimplify.cc (gimplify_scan_omp_clauses): Remove
	simdlen clause with a sorry when it has a scaled modifier.
	* omp-simd-clone.cc (simd_clone_clauses_extract): Likewise.
	* tree-core.h (enum omp_clause_code): Update comment for
	OMP_CLAUSE_SIMDLEN.
	* tree-pretty-print.cc (dump_omp_clause): Handle scaled
	modifier to simdlen.
	(dump_omp_context_selector): Fix dumping of simd trait.
	* tree.cc (omp_clause_num_ops): OMP_CLAUSE_SIMDLEN takes
	now three operands.
	* tree.h (OMP_CLAUSE_SIMDLEN_TYPE,
	OMP_CLAUSE_SIMDLEN_DIVISOR): New defines.

gcc/c/ChangeLog:

	* c-parser.cc (c_parser_omp_clause_simdlen): Handle
	simdlen's type and divisor of the scaled modifier.
	* c-typeck.cc (c_finish_omp_clauses): Add comment
	about safelen vs. simdlen with scaled.

gcc/cp/ChangeLog:

	* parser.cc (cp_parser_omp_clause_simdlen): Handle
	simdlen's type and divisor of the scaled modifier.
	* pt.cc (tsubst_omp_clauses): Likewise
	* semantics.cc (finish_omp_clauses): Likewise;
	add comment about safelen vs. simdlen with scaled.

gcc/testsuite/ChangeLog:

	* c-c++-common/gomp/simdlen-scaled-1.c: New test.
	* c-c++-common/gomp/simdlen-scaled-2.c: New test.
	* c-c++-common/gomp/simdlen-scaled-3.c: New test.
	* c-c++-common/gomp/simdlen-scaled-4.c: New test.
	* g++.dg/gomp/simdlen-scaled-1.C: New test.
	* g++.dg/gomp/simdlen-scaled-2.C: New test.

update.title: [committed][RISC-V] Fix one more test fallout from AOP work on RISC-V
update.body:
One more adjustment related to AOP.  I overlooked this testcase this when
testing patches individually earlier today.

We have a splitter that's supposed to recognize cases where we have (x << C1) +
C2 that can be profitably rewritten into (x + C2') << C1.  After the AOP
changes that splitter is firing in a case where we don't want it.  In
particular when Zbkb is enabled and the shift count is half the word size.
That scenario is tailor made for the pack family in Zbkb.

This patch adjusts the condition for the splitter so that it doesn't apply in
that case.

This was part of the kit that tested overnight.  SO it's been through bootstrap
and regression test as well as testing on riscv64-elf and riscv32-elf.

gcc/
	* config/riscv/riscv.md ((x << C1) + C2 splitter): Do not
	trigger for Zbkb when C1 is half the word size.
update.author: Jeff Law

update.title: [RISC-V] Fix pack* tests for RISC-V after any-or-plus changes
update.body:
The RISC-V port has had a handful of scan-asm failures since the most recent
any-or-plus patches.  This isn't a huge surprise.  This is the first of a few
patches to get regression testing happy again.

This particular patch focuses on the pack family.  They're a poster-child for
AOP in the sense we've going to have an operation like IOR/XOR/PLUS where the
two inputs are known to have zero overlap in set bits.  With generic parts of
the compiler steering towards PLUS, the explicit IOR matching RTL no longer
works.  Fixing these is pretty simple, mostly a matter of creating a code
iterator and using it in the pack patterns.

Additionally, there's costing code that needs to be updated for the new forms
that are showing up.  When the pack instructions were added we had to special
case them in riscv_rtx_costs or they'd get horribly (5X reality) costed and
combine would reject.  We just copy that over to the PLUS handling.

This stands on its own regardless of how we're steering AOP as it merely
supports the additional valid forms.

This fixes all the pack* failures in the default test runs for riscv32-elf and
riscv64-elf.  It's been bootstrapped and regression tested on the k3 and c920
as part of the larger set of patches (k1 is still in progress, but not
expecting problems).

gcc/
	* config/riscv/iterators.md (oxp): New code iterator.
	* config/riscv/crypto.md (pack patterns and splitters): Accept
	oxp in matching RTL.  Fix whitespace goofs.  Generate the PLUS
	forms when possible in splitters.
	* config/riscv/riscv.cc (riscv_rtx_cost, case PLUS): Handle
	PLUS form of pack instructions.
	(riscv_move_integer): Trivial adjustment for crypto.md changes.
update.author: Jeff Law
